claims.claim: LLY's current causal chain runs from incretin/oncology/neuroscience assets through regulatory approval and manufacturing capacity to treatment access and patient outcomes; recent FDA oncology conversion is realized capability, while acquired neuroscience assets remain optionality rather than realized output.

The principal successor bottlenecks are manufacturing/access for high-volume metabolic therapies and commercial adoption/clinical conversion for newer oncology and neuroscience assets; regulatory approval alone does not remove reimbursement, capacity, uptake or trial-conversion constraints.

The thesis remains scenario-robust only if LLY can convert pipeline breadth and manufacturing investment into durable treated-patient volume despite pricing pressure and substitutes; evidence of persistent access constraints, failed clinical conversion, or superior substitute efficacy/cost would falsify that robustness.

factors.name: bottleneck control
factors.basis: Manufacturing expansion can relieve supply constraints, but access/reimbursement and execution remain successor bottlenecks.

factors.name: scenario robustness
factors.basis: Diversified metabolic, oncology and neuroscience pathways reduce single-asset dependence, but clinical conversion and adoption remain uncertain.

factors.name: substitution resilience
factors.basis: Pipeline breadth provides resilience while competing incretin and oncology approaches can pressure share, price and access.

causalEdges.to: human health outcomes and durable economics

risks.risk: Capacity expansion can shift rather than eliminate the bottleneck toward affordability, reimbursement and demand conversion.

unknowns.unknown: Durable launch share, reimbursement breadth and acquired neuroscience clinical conversion are not yet established.

claims.claim: Current evidence supports execution progress but does not justify treating approval, acquisition or pipeline breadth as guaranteed durable revenue; uptake, pricing/reimbursement, clinical conversion and capital-allocation execution remain live uncertainties.

No present evidence in the reviewed lineage establishes an accounting, governance or dilution defect severe enough to block Beta closure; those dimensions should remain explicit unknowns unless source-addressed evidence establishes a contradiction.

A material falsifier would be evidence that realized-price erosion, access limits, manufacturing underutilization, clinical failures or superior substitutes prevent volume/pipeline gains from converting into durable economics.

factors.name: confidence inflation
factors.basis: Regulatory and acquisition milestones can be over-read as commercial or earnings certainty.

factors.name: pricing and reimbursement
factors.basis: Existing lineage explicitly identifies realized-price pressure and reimbursement uncertainty.

factors.name: capital allocation execution
factors.basis: Manufacturing commitments and acquisition activity increase execution demands without proving returns.

risks.risk: Pricing/reimbursement pressure can offset volume growth.
Pipeline and acquired-asset clinical conversion can fail.
Manufacturing and acquisition capital may not earn expected returns.
Competing metabolic and oncology technologies can weaken share or pricing power.

unknowns.unknown: Current source-addressed accounting quality, dilution, customer/payer concentration and governance evidence were not present in the reviewed Beta lineage; absence is not treated as a defect.
